recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-41606 unless a later work group decision changes the OperationDefinition parameter token convention again.
issue_request: FHIR-41606 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for R6. It noted that the OperationDefinition.parameter.name comment required names to start with a letter even though many operation parameter names begin with "_", and the accepted resolution changed the comment to permit either a lowercase letter or underscore as the first character.
initial_application: The accepted wording was already applied by commit 75af205d96d52bc67e9df35f96e8c1acb4615c42, 'FHIR-41606 Broken naming convention for OperationDefinition.parameter', which changed source/operationdefinition/structuredefinition-OperationDefinition.xml from the old letter-only wording to the current 'or underscore' wording. Current blame for the comment line points to that commit.
additional_context: OperationDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, assigned to the conformance category, and has a normative version entry, confirming the inspected XML StructureDefinition is in current build scope. FHIR Infrastructure WGM 202401 minutes record jira:FHIR-41606 Persuasive with motion Gino Canessa/Rick Geimer: 21-0-1. No relevant Zulip discussion, later conflicting decision, or remaining in-build source occurrence of the old wording was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source edit was made because the current authoritative source already matches the Jira resolution and no parallel in-build source location still contains the rejected wording.
